- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.5), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 1–2% in those periods.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 18-day mean is > 70.0, forecast should be adjusted upward toward it by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model often misses the reversal; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift within 2–3 days.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.2 for 5+ days), model tends to overfit recent trends; apply smoothing or reduce volatility weight by 20–30%.
